resources.string: Held. This is not a live reading.
Measuring against your reference surface, not level.
Hold still — a moving phone cannot measure an angle.
This device has no fused gravity sensor, so readings settle more slowly.
This device has no motion sensor, so it cannot measure angles.
Not calibrated. Phones typically read a few tenths of a degree off, which is more than the level mark allows for.
Calibrated for flat use. Readings taken against a wall are only partly corrected.
Calibrating takes about twenty seconds and removes the error built into every phone. Worth doing before you trust a reading.
Hold the phone still, then set the reference.
Put the phone on a flat surface. It does not need to be level — the second step cancels whatever slope it has.
Step 1 of 2 — lay the phone down and hold still.
Step 2 of 2 — now turn the phone 180° flat on the same spot. Do not lift it or turn it over.
Calibrated. Your device reads %1$s° off, and the surface you used is %2$s° from level.
The phone moved during a reading. Try again, keeping it still.
That did not look like a flat 180° turn. Rotate the phone on the spot without lifting it or turning it over.
That produced a result too large to be a real device error. Try again on a flat surface, turning the phone 180° flat.
Those readings could not be used. Try again on a flat surface.
